chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ubeys ibn Hisham, from Husayn ibn Ahmad Al-Minqari, from Yunus ibn Zabyan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
From the Sunnah is wearing the ring.
ai.seo_question: What is the religious ruling on wearing a ring in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the wearing of a ring as a recommended practice (Sunnah), reflecting the Prophet’s and Imams’ adherence to customary social norms while distinguishing their identity. In Shia tradition, this act is often linked to the sealing of documents and serves as a symbol of authority and continuity with the Prophetic legacy, as seen in the famous seal of Imam Ali bearing the inscription 'Ali is the Friend of God.'

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ubeys Bin Hisham, form Husayn Bin Ahmad Al Minqary, from Yunus Bin Zabyan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘From the Sunnah, is wearing of the ring’.
en.sarwar: 3. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufiy from ‘Ubays ibn Hisham from Husayn ibn Ahmad al-Minqariy from Yunus ibn Zabayan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Wearing the ring (insignia) is of the noble tradition.’”
